Replace CPR numbers with random serial numbers

Source: R/pseudo_cpr.R
pseudo_cpr.Rd

Gives every distinct CPR number a serial number, 1 to the number of distinct values, in random order. The same CPR number gets the same serial number throughout the vector, so persons can still be followed across rows, but the number itself carries nothing about the person.

Usage

pseudo_cpr(x, seed = NULL)

Arguments

x

A vector of CPR numbers. Values are matched after the same cleaning as clean_cpr(), so "010100-4007" and "101004007" get the same serial number as "0101004007".

seed

Optional single whole number. With a seed, the same input gives the same serial numbers on every run; the global random number stream is left as it was. Without one, every call draws anew.

Value

An integer vector of the same length as x.

Details

Why random order. Numbering in sorted order would make the serial number follow the birth date, the first six digits of the CPR number. Numbering in order of appearance would tie it to the row order of the source file. A random order avoids both.

No key is kept. The mapping exists only for the duration of the call and is not returned. Two calls therefore give unrelated serial numbers, also on overlapping data. To link several tables, pseudonymise them in one call, for example on the bound key columns, or join first and pseudonymise the result. A fixed seed reproduces the numbering only for exactly the same input; it is not a key that links different data sets.

Pseudonymous, not anonymous. Replacing the identifier does not make the data anonymous in the sense of the GDPR. Birth date, sex, municipality and other columns can still single out a person. Derive what you need with add_cpr_info() before the CPR column is replaced, and remove the original column afterwards.

Missing values, and values that are empty after cleaning, stay NA. Malformed values that are not empty get a serial number like any other value; check them first with diagnose_cpr().

See also

diagnose_cpr(), clean_cpr()

Examples

x <- c("0101004007", "1111111118", "010100-4007", NA, "101004007")
pseudo_cpr(x)
#> [1]  1  2  1 NA  1
pseudo_cpr(x, seed = 1)
#> [1]  1  2  1 NA  1

# Typical use: derive what is needed, then replace the identifier
# df |>
#   add_cpr_info(pnr, bday, sex) |>
#   dplyr::mutate(id = pseudo_cpr(pnr), pnr = NULL)
